newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia oil producers winning export share - ministry.
newsitem.headline: Russia oil producers winning export share - ministry.

text.p: Russian oil producers are reaping the benefits of the Fuel and Energy Ministry's attempts to regulate oil exports, the ministry's InfoTEK agency said in an analysis appearing in its latest monthly bulletin.

The ministry said that steps taken to limit the amount of oil exported outside the Commonwealth of Independent States for state needs had given oil producers the opportunity to export more of their crude abroad.

"The consequences for oil companies and joint ventures of the decisive step taken by the government to limit exports for state needs are already visible today," InfoTEK said in an analysis of the oil export market.
"Now they (oil producers) have more opportunities to pump their own oil for export, which also allows them to solve financial problems and pay their workers and taxes," it added.
State needs exports, also called federal programmes, aim to help raise cash for state projects. They allow companies to buy oil at home, send it abroad and pay less in taxes and tariffs.
Traders traditionally dominate state needs exports.
InfoTEK said state needs exports were 7.14 million tonnes in the first quarter of 1997, nearly one million tonnes below a target set by a ministry official last month of 8.10 million.
This is itself was a downward revision from the planned 9.20 million tonnes, the official had said.
Russia's overall oil export schedule was increased to 28.94 million tonnes in the first quarter of 1997, up from an original target of 25.70 million, InfoTEK said.
Any gains by oil producers on the Russian oil export market are likely to be at the expense of trading companies.
State needs accounted for 23 percent of Russia's two million barrels per day (bpd) non-CIS crude oil exports last year. Russian output was around six million bpd.
In last month's bulletin, the ministry openly backed producers over traders in the battle for control over lucrative deliveries abroad.
InfoTEK said in its latest publication that new government appointees could lobby for an increase in state need export volumes, in order to boost finances for projects at home.

But it would be difficult for them to push through such changes, because all governmental documents regarding oil exports had to be agreed upon by the inter-departmental commission regulating access to the oil export pipeline system.
InfoTEK said Russian non-CIS oil exports rose 6.2 percent to 16.55 million tonnes in the first two months of the year, the latest period for which data was available.
The figure included Russian deliveries to the Baltics, which are not a part of the CIS, it said.
InfoTEK also said LUKoil , Russia's biggest oil producer, exported 2.67 million tonnes of crude outside the CIS in the first quarter, and joint ventures with foreign companies 2.12 million tonnes.
Exports by Russia's second largest oil company by output, YUKOS, were 1.82 million tonnes in the first quarter and those by Surgutneftegaz, the third largest producer, 1.56 million.
